fatal_errors: The proposed mechanical-alloying/SPS route does not reconstruct the target liquid-metal dealloying method using molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It misses the essential selective replacement of Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels and the resulting directionally aligned, bicontinuous RHEA–Cu architecture.
It omits the W-rich interfacial passivation layer and incorrectly frames homogeneous mixing and suppressed phase separation as the desired mechanism.

The cited evidence demonstrates mechanical alloying and SPS of a Cu-free RHEA, not scalable RHEA–Cu composite formation, machine-learning optimization, or stability against refractory–Cu immiscibility.
No evidence supports the claimed large-scale capability, improved thermal transport, or nuclear-environment performance.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad challenge of combining RHEAs with Cu and proposes a testable processing alternative, but it is scientifically disconnected from the target method and mechanism. The target exploits precursor segregation rather than eliminating it: molten-Cu liquid-metal dealloying selectively removes Ti-rich interdendritic material, preserves continuous refractory-rich ligaments, and forms aligned Cu channels stabilized by an approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer. None of these defining features, conditions, or outcomes appears in the generated hypothesis. Its experiment could compare process optimization strategies, but it does not directly test large-scale penetration, directional architecture, interfacial passivation, thermal conductivity, or irradiation response. Moreover, E1–E3 support general RHEA properties and MA/SPS processing of a Cu-free alloy only; they do not validate AI optimization or the proposed RHEA–Cu route.
